project_name: JSE Money Market ISIN Issuance Service

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary business outcomes and success criteria you want this ISIN issuance service to achieve—for example, in terms of turnaround time, reduction of manual effort, operational control, and support for same-day trading, clearing, and settlement?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main outcome is that participants can get an ISIN issued, amended, or removed fast enough to keep money-market instruments moving through the market without delay. We want the process to be efficient enough that same-day trading, clearing, and settlement are supported, so turnaround has to be measured in minutes rather than hours or days. We also want to cut down manual handling significantly, while keeping strong control over the records so the market data stays accurate, auditable, and reliable.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which stakeholder groups will be involved in this service end-to-end, and what role does each group play in submitting, reviewing, approving, or processing ISIN create, amend, and delete requests?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main groups are the Money Market Forum participants, STRATE as the submission and routing channel, and the JSE as the authority that issues and maintains the ISIN record. Participants originate the request and provide the supporting details, STRATE receives and passes it through in the agreed format, and the JSE validates, approves, and updates the identifier record. In some cases internal operations or market control staff at the JSE may review exceptions or fixes, but that would be part of the controlled processing on our side.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which specific request types should the service support beyond create, amend, and delete—for example, are there different ISIN issuance or maintenance scenarios, and what details or variations need to be captured for each?
turns.interviewee_utterance: At the core, we definitely need create, amend, and delete, and those cover the normal lifecycle for these money-market instruments. There may be maintenance variations within amend, like changing issue details, maturity details, or participant-related information, but I’d need to verify the exact fields with the business team. We are not looking for a lot of extra request types unless there is a clear operational need; the aim is to keep the workflow simple and controlled.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What exact service-level targets should this ISIN service meet for create, amend, and delete requests—for example, target response or completion times, any same-day cutoff times, availability expectations, and whether different priorities or escalation timelines apply for normal versus exception cases?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We need the service to respond quickly enough to support same-day market activity, so the practical target is same-business-day completion for standard requests, with turnaround measured in minutes or a few hours rather than overnight. I don’t have a formally agreed cutoff time yet, but there will almost certainly need to be a clear operating window and a late-day escalation path for urgent cases. For exceptions, we’d expect longer handling only where manual review is required, but those should be tightly controlled and tracked so they don’t disrupt trading or settlement.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What operating hours and submission cutoff rules should govern this service—for example, when is the service open for normal processing, what is the latest time a create/amend/delete request can be received for same-day completion, and what should happen to requests submitted after cutoff or near end-of-day?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The service should broadly align with the market’s business day, so normal processing would be during trading and settlement hours on JSE business days. I don’t have the exact cutoff time confirmed, but there will need to be a point after which same-day completion can no longer be guaranteed. Anything received after cutoff, or too close to end-of-day to process safely, would need to roll to the next business day unless it is specifically escalated and approved as an exception.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For create, amend, and delete requests submitted through STRATE, what acknowledgement and status-update behavior do you need from the JSE—for example, what statuses should participants see, when should acknowledgements be sent, and how should standard requests differ from exception cases in terms of notifications or progress updates?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We need an immediate acknowledgement that the request was received by the service, so participants aren’t left wondering whether STRATE or the JSE got it. After that, they should be able to see a clear status progression, something like received, under review, completed, or rejected, with the final outcome returned as soon as the request is processed. For exception cases, I’d expect additional update points while it is being manually reviewed, but standard requests should be as close to straight-through as possible with minimal chatter.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What message format, transport protocol, and security controls should STRATE use when submitting create, amend, and delete requests to the JSE—for example, are there specific payload standards, encryption or signing requirements, and authentication or authorization rules for participants and JSE users?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We definitely need a structured electronic message format so the requests are consistent and can be processed automatically, but I don’t have the exact standard confirmed yet. Security-wise, the transport has to be encrypted and access tightly authenticated, with only approved participants able to submit through STRATE and only authorized JSE users able to process or override requests. If signing or message-level validation is required as well, I’d expect that to be part of the controlled interface, but I’d need to check the technical standard with the integration and security teams.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which technical message standard and transport protocol should be used for requests submitted through STRATE, and what specific message authentication or integrity controls are required—for example, should the interface use a defined industry standard, digital signatures, message-level validation, or other non-repudiation controls?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I can’t confirm a specific industry standard or transport protocol from memory, so I’d need to verify that with the STRATE and JSE technical teams. What I can say is that we would expect strong message integrity and non-repudiation controls, so some combination of authenticated transport, message validation, and audit traceability will be required. If digital signatures are part of the agreed interface standard, then yes, those would need to be enforced end to end.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For the ISIN records and related request data, what specific data entities should the service store and manage, and how should each record move through its lifecycle from creation through amendment and deletion, including any rules for retaining historical or audit-related records?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The service should store the ISIN record itself, the request record, and the audit trail linking who submitted it, when it was submitted, and what action was taken. In practice, each record needs to move through a controlled lifecycle so that a create establishes the identifier, an amend updates the active details without losing the prior version, and a delete marks the record as inactive rather than wiping out the history. I’d expect historical and audit records to be retained for compliance and traceability, but the exact retention period would need to be confirmed with the records and regulatory team.
